items.title: RIFT: Reordered Instruction Following Testbed To Evaluate Instruction Following in Singular Multistep Prompt Structures
items.title_zh: RIFT：在单一多步提示结构中评估指令遵循的重排测试平台
items.summary: RIFT uses rephrased Jeopardy! question-answer pairs to compare linear prompts with jumping prompts that preserve content but require non-sequential traversal. Across 10,000 evaluations of six open-source LLMs, accuracy dropped by up to 72% under jumping conditions, with about half of failures traced to instruction-order violations and semantic drift.

items.title: Tricky$^2$: Towards a Benchmark for Evaluating Human and LLM Error Interactions
items.title_zh: Tricky²：评估人类与 LLM 错误交互的基准
items.summary: Tricky² augments the TrickyBugs corpus of human-written defects with errors injected by GPT-5 and OpenAI-oss-20b across C++, Python and Java programs, using taxonomy-guided prompting. The resulting splits cover human-only, LLM-only and human+LLM errors, enabling analysis of mixed-origin error behavior, multi-bug repair robustness and reliability in hybrid code.

items.title: Reflect: Transparent Principle-Guided Reasoning for Constitutional Alignment at Scale
items.title_zh: Reflect：面向大规模宪法对齐的透明原则引导推理
items.summary: Reflect is an inference-time constitutional-alignment framework that requires no training or data, combining a constitution-conditioned base response with self-evaluation, self-critique and final revision. The authors report improved conformance to diverse principles without sacrificing factual reasoning, particular effectiveness at reducing rare but significant violations, and useful training data for later fine-tuning.

items.title: TEA-Bench: A Systematic Benchmarking of Tool-enhanced Emotional Support Dialogue Agent
items.title_zh: TEA-Bench：工具增强情绪支持对话智能体的系统评测基准
items.summary: TEA-Bench is an interactive benchmark for tool-augmented emotional-support agents, with realistic scenarios, an MCP-style tool environment and process-level metrics for support quality and factual grounding. Across nine LLMs, tool augmentation generally improved support quality and reduced hallucination, but gains were strongly capacity-dependent, and supervised fine-tuning on the released TEA-Dialog data generalized poorly.

items.title: The $\mathbf{P}$-Completeness of Inverted Index Traversal: On the Complexity of Evaluating Boolean Query DAGs
items.title_zh: 倒排索引遍历的 P-完全性：布尔查询 DAG 的求值复杂性
items.summary: The paper formalizes a DAG-based retrieval language and proves that evaluating its Boolean queries over an inverted index is P-complete, exposing worst-case exponential blowup for document-at-a-time evaluation and a universal-scan penalty for term-at-a-time materialization. It introduces ComputePN, a sparsity-aware algorithm with a positive-negative dual representation that bounds evaluation time to O(|Q|·|U_active|).

items.title: alsk1992/CloddsBot
items.title_zh: CloddsBot：开源 AI 交易代理
items.summary: CloddsBot is a self-hosted open-source AI trading agent built on Claude in TypeScript that operates across more than 1,000 markets, including Polymarket, Kalshi, Binance, Hyperliquid, Solana DEXs and five EVM chains. It scans for edge, executes trades, manages risk and includes an agent commerce protocol for machine-to-machine payments.
